title: WeMacro Bluetooth manual move during a batch stalls the batch countdown
description: In indigo_mac_drivers/focuser_wemacro_bt/indigo_focuser_wemacro_bt.m the FOCUSER_STEPS change handler accepts a move while an X_RAIL_EXECUTE batch is running (X_RAIL_EXECUTE_PROPERTY in INDIGO_BUSY_STATE) and sends the move command to the rail. The notification handler (didUpdateValueForCharacteristic) checks FOCUSER_STEPS BUSY first and handles batch notifications only in the else branch, so while the move is BUSY the 0xf7 step notifications of the batch are dropped and the 0xf5/0xf6 notifications are attributed to the move. The COUNT countdown then no longer matches the rail and may never reach 0, leaving X_RAIL_EXECUTE BUSY; since ticket a2513f61-8af8-4ff2-a950-7bf0658d19a0 a BUSY batch refuses new batch requests, so only FOCUSER_ABORT_MOTION recovers it. Expected: the two operations are mutually exclusive, consistently with the portable sibling indigo_drivers/focuser_wemacro: a FOCUSER_STEPS request while a batch is running, and an X_RAIL_EXECUTE request while a move is running, is refused without sending commands to the rail or changing the running operation's state; abort keeps working for both. Add hardware-free regression coverage in indigo_test/unit/test_focuser_wemacro_bt.py and increment DRIVER_VERSION. Found by the reviewer of ticket a2513f61 as a pre-existing, out-of-scope issue; how the physical rail reacts to a move command during a batch was not measured.

outcome.summary: Defect confirmed in source: didUpdateValueForCharacteristic (indigo_focuser_wemacro_bt.m:244-258) serves FOCUSER_STEPS BUSY first, so a move accepted during a batch swallowed 0xf7 and took 0xf5/0xf6. Fix: INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF guards at :389 (FOCUSER_STEPS refused while X_RAIL_EXECUTE BUSY) and :442 (X_RAIL_EXECUTE refused while FOCUSER_STEPS BUSY), both before indigo_property_copy_values and before any delegate cmd; matches portable sibling indigo_focuser_wemacro.c:629/642. indigo_reject_change (indigo_bus.c:1325-1350) sets the non-BUSY requested property ALERT with its unchanged values (documented use, indigo_bus.h:984-992); the next accepted request of that property resets it (STEPS :391-392, EXECUTE :448), and the running operation's state is untouched. Base focuser class does not handle FOCUSER_STEPS changes (driver returns at :400), so no bypass. Exit paths: STEPS leaves BUSY via 0xf5/0xf6, abort (:409) and base disconnect reset (indigo_focuser_driver.c:184); EXECUTE via notification, abort (:407) and loss (:196-197). The guards cannot leave both BUSY; abort still ends both. DRIVER_VERSION 0x02000006 -> 0x02000007. Tests: 4/4 pass; against master's driver source in a scratch copy both new assertions fail (rejects == 1 at probe lines 84 and 54). Non-blocking test notes: the mocked INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF ignores which property is rejected, and the X_RAIL_EXECUTE probe mocks copy_values as a no-op so guard-before-copy order is only covered for FOCUSER_STEPS.

history.text: Reproduced: new assertions failed on the unmodified driver (X_RAIL_EXECUTE and FOCUSER_STEPS requests were accepted while the other was BUSY). Fix: INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF guards in both handlers (as portable sibling), DRIVER_VERSION 0x02000007. After fix test_focuser_wemacro_bt passes 4/4. Physical rail reaction not measured.
